**Finding: compliant (sits at the fallback).**

- **Vendor keeps its own tools/know-how:** §7.1.1 (p0427–p0428) and §5.6.1 leave each Party owning its own inventions and IP — the permitted outcome, not a deviation.
- **Customer licence:** §5.1.3(a) grants AbbVie an exclusive, worldwide (Territory = "the entire world") licence to Exploit the Licensed Compounds/Products, sublicensable through multiple tiers under §5.3, which on expiry becomes "non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable" (§12.1.2). Royalties during the Royalty Term are the deal price, noted only in the rationale.
- **No assignment of our IP/data to Harpoon:** AbbVie owns Regulatory Documentation in the Territory (§3.8.2(c)) and the Product Trademarks (§7.6); Harpoon's only grant-back (§5.2) is limited to Developing and Manufacturing "solely to the extent necessary… to perform its obligations… under the Initial Development Plan" — service delivery, satisfying the Customer-data element.
- **Joint IP:** §7.1.2 creates joint ownership (short of the preferred "no joint ownership"), but each Party may Exploit "without a duty of seeking consent from or accounting to the other Party", so it is not walk-away territory and the fallback has no such element.

No redline proposed. The redacted carve-outs at the end of §7.1.2 and in the §12.7.1 reversion licence should be confirmed commercially.
